source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} after{H310} this, at that time{H6256}, he saw{H7200} the companies{H2274} and went up{H5927} the mountain{H2022} and sat{H3427}; and his disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to him.

one_way_hebrew: ויעל ההר — 'he went up the mountain' in Sinai's own verbs (Exod 24:15, ויעל משה אל ההר; 19:3): the Torah-teaching that follows opens with Moshe's ascent formula, and the teacher sits (וישב) as one giving Torah.

ויקריבו — the disciples 'were brought near' (קרב, H7126) — the Sanctuary's approach-verb: those who receive the teaching draw near as offerers draw near the altar (the same root opens the qorban instruction of vv. 23-24).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק י״ג (Perek 13) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (5:1): ויקריבו] ויקרבו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And he opened{H6605} his mouth{H6310} and spoke{H1696} to them, saying{H559}:

one_way_hebrew: ויפתח פיו — the wisdom-teacher's opening formula (Ps 78:2, אפתחה במשל פי; Prov 31:26; Job 3:1): in Hebrew this is how a mashal-discourse begins.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:2): לאמר omitted in EF.

verses.translation: (Happy{H835} are the lowly{H8217} of spirit{H7307}, for theirs is the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}.)

one_way_hebrew: אשרי — the Psalter's beatitude-word (Ps 1:1), opening the whole run as the Psalms open. שפלי רוח — 'the LOWLY of spirit': Isa 57:15 verbatim (ושפל רוח — with whom the High and Lofty One dwells) and Prov 29:23 (ושפל רוח יתמך כבוד). Greek's πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι ('poor in spirit') has puzzled readers for centuries; the Hebrew is a fixed scriptural phrase with its promise attached.
textual_notes: Howard prints the verse in parentheses: it is missing from the base ms (British Library Add. 26964) and from BCDEFG — his apparatus (5:3): 'Whole vs] omit Brit. Lib. ms BCDEFG; text = A.' The verse stands here from ms A.

verses.translation: Happy{H835} are those who wait{H2442}, for they shall be comforted{H5162}.

one_way_hebrew: 'Happy are those who WAIT' — not 'those who mourn' (Greek οἱ πενθοῦντες). The Hebrew is Isaiah's own beatitude: אשרי כל חוכי לו — 'happy are all who WAIT for him' (Isa 30:18) — answered by Isaiah's own comfort: נחמו נחמו עמי (Isa 40:1). חכה (H2442) and נחם (H5162) are Isaiah's paired words, and חכה is the very verb of endurance in this gospel's discourse (24:13, 'whoever WAITS until the end will be saved'). The Greek kept the comfort and lost the waiting.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:4): vs 4 omitted in G, placed after vs 5 in A; החוכים] הברכים A.
The circulating transcription inserts שהם before שינוחמו; the scan reads אשרי החוכים שינוחמו — corrected here.

verses.translation: (Happy{H835} are the meek{H6035}, for they shall inherit{H3423} the earth{H776}.)

one_way_hebrew: Ps 37:11 word for word: וענוים יירשו ארץ — the beatitude IS the psalm-line, quoted whole. Greek translates the same verse; the Hebrew simply is it.
textual_notes: Howard prints the verse in parentheses: missing from the base ms and BCDEFG; text from ms A (apparatus 5:5: 'vs 5] omit Brit. Lib. ms BCDEFG; text = A').

GREEK 5:6-7 HAVE NO COUNTERPART IN ANY SHEM TOV MS: Howard's apparatus — 'vs 6] omit all mss; vs 7] omit all mss.' The text runs directly from v. 5 to v. 8: no 'hunger and thirst after righteousness,' no 'merciful obtain mercy.' (The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries both verses; the Shem Tov family carries neither.)

verses.translation: Happy{H835} are the pure{H2134} of heart{H3820}, for they shall see{H7200} Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: זך — Job's purity word (Job 8:6, אם זך וישר אתה; 33:9) with Prov 20:11 (זך וישר); the pure-hearted seeing God answers Ps 24:4-6 (בר לבב — the clean-hearted ascend and seek his face) and Ps 73:1.
textual_notes: First אלקים of the chapter — the ms's reverent ק-spelling (see 1:23).
Howard's apparatus (5:8): vs 8 omitted in G; אלקים] אלים A.

verses.translation: Happy{H835} are the pursuers{H7291} of peace{H7965}, for they shall be called{H7121} sons{H1121} of Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: רודפי שלום — 'PURSUERS of peace': Ps 34:15's command, בקש שלום ורדפהו ('seek peace and pursue it'), and the rabbis' epithet for Aharon (Avot 1:12, אוהב שלום ורודף שלום). Greek εἰρηνοποιοί ('peace-MAKERS') is a different word entirely — and it severs the hinge to the next verse, which only the Hebrew's root can carry.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:9): אלקים] אלים A; שלום] השלום G.

verses.translation: Happy{H835} are the pursued{H7291} for righteousness{H6664}, for theirs is the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: רודפי שלום (v. 9) → הנרדפים (v. 10): the pursuers of peace become the pursued — one Hebrew root (רדף) hinges the two beatitudes into a single turn of thought, and v. 11's ירדפו carries it on. Greek uses unrelated words (εἰρηνοποιοί / δεδιωγμένοι) and the chain vanishes: the catchword structure exists only in Hebrew.

verses.translation: Happy{H835} are you when they pursue{H7291} and revile{H1442} you, and say{H559} against you every{H3605} evil{H7451} for my sake{H1157} — but they lie{H3576}.

one_way_hebrew: ויגדפו (H1442) — the reviling of the Rab-shakeh against the living God (2 Kgs 19:6, 22, גדף): the word for blasphemous abuse. And רדף a third time — the chain of vv. 9-11 runs on one root.

verses.translation: Rejoice{H7797} and be glad{H8055}, for your reward{H7939} is exceedingly{H3966} great{H7227} in heaven{H8064}; for thus they pursued{H7291} the prophets{H5030}.

one_way_hebrew: שישו ושמחו — the doubled joy-pair of the Psalter and Isaiah (Ps 40:17, ישישו וישמחו בך — 'let all who seek thee rejoice and be glad'; Isa 65:18). And שכרכם רב מאד — the promise to Avram nearly verbatim: שכרך הרבה מאד ('your reward is exceedingly great,' Gen 15:1). רדף a fourth time closes the run.
translation_notes: ושמחו — the transcription reads ושחמו (letter-order slip); the scan reads ושמחו, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:12): רב omitted in EFG; ששכרכם] כי שכרכם EF; הנביאים] + שלפניכם A ('who were before you', as the Greek).

verses.translation: At that time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: You are salt{H4417} in the world{H5769}. If the salt is annulled{H988} as to its taste{H2940}, with what{H4100} will it be salted{H4414}? It is worth{H7737} nothing{H369}, except to be cast{H7993} outside{H2351} to be a trampling{H4823} of feet{H7272}.

one_way_hebrew: מרמס (H4823) — Isaiah's judgment-word for what is trodden down (Isa 5:5, the vineyard given למרמס; 7:25; 10:6; 28:18): what loses its office becomes mirmas. Greek καταπατεῖσθαι translates the picture and loses the prophetic term.

בעת ההיא אמר — 'at that time he said': the Hebrew storyteller's resumptive formula, recurring at vv. 17, 20, 25 and dividing the sermon into Shem Tov's own perek-units — the seams of a Hebrew composition.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק י״ד (Perek 14) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (5:13): בחוץ] לחוץ AEF; שיושלך] שיושלח A; רגלים] לרגלים ABDEF, omit G.

verses.translation: You are a luminary{H3974} in the world{H5769}. A city{H5892} built{H1129} on the mountain{H2022} cannot{H3201} be hidden{H5641}.

one_way_hebrew: מאור (H3974) — not אור ('light') but MAOR, the light-BEARER: Gen 1:14-16's word for the sun, moon, and stars ('God made the two great מאורות'), and the Sanctuary's lamp-oil (Exod 25:6, שמן למאר). 'You are the luminary of the world' places the disciples where Genesis put the lights of heaven and where the Torah put the Menorah's flame — burning from within, not reflecting. Greek φῶς flattens luminary to light; v. 15's מנורה completes the Sanctuary picture.

verses.translation: They do not kindle{H1814} a lamp{H5216} to set{H7760} it in a hidden{H5641} place{H4725} where it cannot shine{H215}; rather they set it on the menorah{H4501}, to give light{H215} to all the sons{H1121} of the house{H1004}.

one_way_hebrew: נר... על המנורה... להאיר — lamp, lampstand, and purpose-clause are the Sanctuary's own (Exod 25:37: 'he shall light its lamps — נרתיה — that they may give light,' והאיר). The household scene is the Tabernacle writ small; Greek λυχνία is furniture, מנורה is the Menorah.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:15): להשים] לשים B; לכל] כל DEFG.

verses.translation: So{H3651} let your luminary{H3974} shine{H215} before{H6440} every man{H120}, to show them{H7200} your good{H2896} deeds{H4639}, which are praised{H7623} and give honor{H3513} to your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

greek_deviations: In the Hebrew the DEEDS themselves 'are praised and give honor to your Father' — the glory flows through the works; in the Greek the onlookers 'glorify your Father.' A small hinge with a real difference: the Hebrew makes the deeds the bearers of the honor.

verses.translation: At that time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: Do not think{H2803} that I came{H935} to annul{H6565} Torah{H8451}, but to complete{H7999} it.

one_way_hebrew: להפר... להשלים — the sentence runs on the Torah's own legal pair. הפר (H6565) is the annulment-verb of Num 30 (יפר את נדרה — the husband ANNULS the vow, against הקים, 'confirm, uphold') and of Ps 119:126 (הפרו תורתך — 'they have ANNULLED thy Torah'). 'I came not to annul but to complete' is vow-law language: not abolition versus observance but annulment versus confirmation — and the next two verses close the frame with the pair's other pole, קום: 'everything shall be ESTABLISHED' (יתקיים, v. 18), 'the one who UPHOLDS' (המקיים, v. 19). Greek καταλῦσαι/πληρῶσαι cannot carry the Num 30 pairing. The completion deepens the command; it does not dissolve a letter of it — as v. 18 says in so many words.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:17): mss A and D expand ('the Torah or the Prophets I came not to annul...'); שבאתי omitted in EF.

verses.translation: In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you: until{H5704} heaven{H8064} and earth{H776} [pass], one{H259} letter{H226} or one point shall not be annulled{H988} from the Torah{H8451} or from the Prophets{H5030}, for everything{H3605} shall be established{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: אות אחת ונקודה אחת — 'one LETTER and one POINT': the Hebrew scribe's own units, the letter and the dot of his page. Greek names a GREEK letter (ἰῶτα) — and ms A corrects it to יוד ('one yod'), the pull of a Hebrew original showing even inside the manuscript tradition.
יתקיים — 'shall be ESTABLISHED' (קום): the confirming pole of Num 30's הפר/הקים pair (see v. 17). Nothing annulled, everything confirmed — the word of our God stands (יקום), Isa 40:8.
greek_deviations: The base reads elliptically עד שמים וארץ — 'until heaven and earth' without a verb; mss A and BCDEFG supply שימושו/שמושו ('DEPART'), the verb of Isa 54:10 (ההרים ימושו — 'the mountains shall depart, but my kindness shall not depart') — where Greek has παρέλθῃ ('pass away'). Howard renders 'until heaven and earth (depart).'
The guarantee extends to the PROPHETS — מהתורה או מהנביאים — where Greek Matthew 5:18 names only the law.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:18): עד] + שימושו A, שמושו BCDEFG; אות] יוד A; תבטל] תתבטל A; מהתורה] מן התורה B; או מהנביאים] ומן הנביאים B; כי omitted in D.

verses.translation: And whoever transgresses{H5674} one word{H3982} of these{H428} commandments{H4687} which I teach{H3925} others{H312} shall be called{H7121} a son{H1121} of vanity{H1892} [in regard to] the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}; but the one who upholds{H6965} and teaches{H3925} [them] shall be called great{H1419} in the kingdom of heaven.

one_way_hebrew: בן הבל — 'a son of HEVEL': Qohelet's word for vapor, what does not last. The Greek grades the transgressor 'least' (ἐλάχιστος); the Hebrew unnames him — a teacher who breaks one word of the commandments is a son of emptiness. Ms D reads קטן ('small'), assimilating to the Greek's grading.

והמקיים — 'the one who UPHOLDS': the rabbis' own phrase for keeping Torah (Avot 4:9, המקיים את התורה) and the third stroke of the הפר/הקים frame (vv. 17-18). The smallest מצוה binds — the verse says of the commandments exactly what v. 18 says of their letters.
translation_notes: The transcription omits שמים after the first מלכות and reads והמקים; the scan reads יקרא מלכות שמים והמקיים — corrected here. The base lacks ב before the first מלכות ('called a son of vanity [of the] kingdom of heaven'); mss ABDEFG read במלכות.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:19): מלכות] במלכות ABDEFG; אשר אלמד] וילמד ABDEFG ('and teaches [men so],' as the Greek); א״] + קטן A ('one SMALL commandment'); בן הבל] קטן D.

verses.translation: At that time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: In truth{H571} I say to you, if your righteousness{H6666} is not greater{H1431}, more{H3148} than the Perushim{H6567} and the sages{H2450}, you shall not enter{H935} the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}.

greek_deviations: 'The Perushim and the SAGES' (החכמים) — Greek has 'the scribes (γραμματέων) and Pharisees.' חכמים is the rabbis' own self-designation, the living term of the Hebrew academy; a Greek translator had no reason to invent it, a Hebrew author no way to avoid it.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ט״ו (Perek 15) begins here.

verses.translation: Have you not heard{H8085} what was said{H559} to the ancients{H6931}: You shall not murder{H7523}, and whoever murders is liable to a judgment{H4941} of death{H4194}?

one_way_hebrew: לא תרצח — Exod 20:13 in its own two words; the appended sentence is the Torah's own penalty (Num 35:16-21). חייב — chayav, the Mishnah's liability-term, which structures this whole section (vv. 21-22) exactly as it structures a Mishnah paragraph: כל העושה X חייב Y. The discourse is halakhic Hebrew in form as well as content.

קדמונים — 'the ancients, those of old' (as in 1 Sam 24:14, משל הקדמני, 'the proverb of the ancients'): the appeal is to received tradition, and vv. 21-48 will distinguish what the Torah says (v. 38, 'in the Torah') from what 'was said' in tradition's name (v. 43).

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: whoever provokes{H3707} his companion{H2270} is liable to judgment{H4941}; and whoever calls{H7121} his brother{H251} 'inferior' shall be liable to judgment before the assembly{H6951}; and whoever calls him 'fool' is liable to the fire{H784} of Gehinnom.

one_way_hebrew: גהינם — the Hebrew place-name itself (גיא הנם, Josh 15:8; the Topheth of Jer 7:31-32); Greek γέεννα transliterates it. חבר (H2270) — the fellow of Ps 119:63, the rabbinic chaver.
greek_deviations: No 'Raca': Greek Matthew preserves an untranslated Semitic insult (ῥακά) it cannot explain; the Hebrew has plain, graded insults — פחות ('inferior') and שוטה (the Mishnah's own word for a fool) — before graded tribunals: המשפט (the court), הקהל (the assembly), אש גהינם. A Hebrew original needs no loanword for its own insult; a Greek translation must carry it as a fossil.

המכעיס לחבירו — 'whoever PROVOKES his companion' (מכעיס, causative): the base text condemns the act of provoking, not the feeling of anger (Greek ὁ ὀργιζόμενος, 'whoever is angry') — and it has no 'without cause' clause for copyists to fight over.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:22): לחבירו] את חברו EF; יחייב] חייב A; למשפט] במשפט BEF.

verses.translation: And if you offer{H7126} your offering{H7133} at the altar{H4196} and remember{H2142} that you had a dispute{H1779} with your companion{H2270}, and he complains{H7481} against you about some matter{H1697} —

one_way_hebrew: קרבן... מזבח... תקריב — Leviticus' own opening (Lev 1:2, אדם כי יקריב מכם קרבן): the instruction presumes the Sanctuary service as valid and continuing — the offering is interrupted for reconciliation and then completed (v. 24), never waved off. דין and מתרעם are the working terms of Hebrew legal life.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:23): ותזכיר] ותזכור ABDEFG; עם חברך דין] transposed in ABDEFG.

verses.translation: leave{H3240} your offering{H7133} there{H8033} before{H6440} the altar{H4196}, and go{H1980} first{H6924} to appease him{H7521}, and afterwards{H310} offer{H7126} your offering.

one_way_hebrew: לרצותו — the appeasement verb is the ALTAR's own acceptance-verb: ונרצה לו ('it shall be ACCEPTED for him,' Lev 1:4). Reconciling the brother is stated in the vocabulary of sacrificial acceptance — the offering cannot be רצוי while the brother is not. And the command ends by commanding the offering: הקרב קרבניך — the altar-service upheld, not annulled (v. 17).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:24): קרבניך (both)] קרבנך ABDEFG; לרצותו קודם] transposed A; כך omitted in ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: See{H7200} that you hasten{H4116} to appease{H7521} your foe{H8130} while walking{H1980} with him on the way{H1870}, lest{H6435} he deliver{H4560} you to the judge{H8199}, and this judge deliver you to the servant{H5650}, to put{H5414} you into the prison-house{H5470}.

one_way_hebrew: בית הסוהר — the phrase has exactly one biblical home: Joseph's prison (Gen 39:20-23; 40:3,5, בית הסהר). The debtor's jail is named with the Joseph-narrative's own word; Greek φυλακή is any guardhouse. And לרצות continues v. 24's acceptance-verb: one Hebrew root binds appeasing the brother at the altar and the adversary on the road.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ט״ז (Perek 16) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (5:25): ראה] יאות ADEFG, ויאות B; שונאך] לשונאך A.

verses.translation: In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you: you shall not come out{H3318} from there{H8033} until{H5704} the last{H314} perutah is given{H5414}.

one_way_hebrew: פרוטה — the Mishnah's smallest coin, its legal threshold of value (שוה פרוטה). Greek has κοδράντης, the Latin quadrans. Each text prices the debt in its own marketplace — and this text's marketplace is the Mishnah's.
translation_notes: באמת — the transcription reads בעמת; the scan reads באמת, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:26): תנתן] תתן ABDG, שתתן EF; אחרונה] האחרונה G.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: You have heard{H8085} what was said{H559} to the ancients{H6931}: You shall not commit adultery{H5003}.

one_way_hebrew: לא תנאף — Exod 20:14 in its own two words.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק יז (Perek 17) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (5:27): לקדמונים omitted in D.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: everyone who sees{H7200} a woman{H802} and covets{H2530} her has already committed adultery{H5003} with her in her heart{H3820}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחמוד — the tenth commandment's own verb: לא תחמד אשת רעך ('you shall not COVET your neighbor's wife,' Exod 20:17; Deut 5:21). The saying reads the seventh commandment through the tenth — adultery begins where coveting begins — an inner-Torah derivation that is visible only when the verb is חמד. Greek ἐπιθυμῆσαι blurs the Decalogue echo. The teaching deepens the commandment; it does not replace it.
greek_deviations: בלבה — 'in HER heart' (the base ms): the coveting pair are joined in the sin — it reaches her heart too. Mss BDEFGH read בלבו ('in his heart'), as the Greek; Howard renders '(his).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:28): בלבה] בלבו BDEFGH; אשה] לאשה ABDEFG; ואני] אני EF.

verses.translation: And if your right{H3225} eye{H5869} entices you{H5496}, gouge it out{H5365} and cast it{H7993} from you.

one_way_hebrew: יסיתך — Deut 13:7's own verb: כי יסיתך אחיך... בסתר ('if your brother ENTICE you secretly' — to serve other gods). In the Hebrew the eye is an enticer in the Deut 13 sense, to be dealt with as ruthlessly as Deut 13 deals with the enticer; Greek σκανδαλίζει ('trips you up') is a stumbling-metaphor with no statute behind it. נקר — the eye-gouging verb itself (Judg 16:21, Samson; 1 Sam 11:2).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:29): עיניך] עינך AD; יסיתך] הסיתך EF; אותה] אותו AB.

verses.translation: And likewise, if your hand{H3027} entices you{H5496}, cut it off{H2852}: better{H2896} for you to lose one{H259} of your limbs than all{H3605} your body{H1480} in Gehinnom.

translation_notes: The Hebrew is compressed ('better that you lose one of your limbs than your whole body in Gehinnom'); mss ABDEFG smooth with משיאבד ('than that [your whole body] perish'). תפסיד ('lose') and אבר ('limb') are rabbinic usage; גוף — the rabbinic body-word (biblical trace at 1 Chr 10:12, גופת).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק י״ח (Perek 18) begins at v. 31.
Howard's apparatus (5:30): מכל] משיאבד כל ABDEFG; מאבריך] מאיבריך B.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: You have heard{H8085} what was said{H559} to the ancients{H6931}: everyone who leaves{H5800} his wife{H802} and sends her away{H7971} is to give{H5414} her a get of severance{H3748} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, libel repudio.

one_way_hebrew: גט כריתות — Deut 24:1's ספר כריתת ('scroll of severance,' H3748) in its living rabbinic form: גט, the Mishnah's word for the document (a whole tractate, Gittin, bears it). And the scribe glosses the Hebrew legal term with the church's Latin — ליבי״ל ריפודייו, libellus repudii — for readers who know Romance legal vocabulary: a Hebrew law-text explaining itself to a Latin land (with מי״רא 2:11, מאריטמה 4:13). The gloss runs outward from the Hebrew, never inward.
textual_notes: The printed לעז carries points and the double-yod ligature; normalized here.
Howard's apparatus (5:31): לקדמונים] לקודמים DEFG; ובלעז] בלעז BE, לעז ADG; the לעז is variously spelled (A די ריפוג׳; omitted in H).

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: everyone who leaves{H5800} his wife{H802} must{H3426} give{H5414} her a get of severance{H3748}; except for a matter{H1697} of adultery{H5004}, HE is the adulterer{H5003}, and he who takes{H3947} her commits adultery{H5003}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew UPHOLDS Deut 24:1: the man who dismisses his wife MUST give her the get — the document is commanded, protecting the woman, not criticized. And the guilt falls on the dismissing man himself: הוא הנואף, 'HE is the adulterer' — where Greek Matthew turns the clause against the woman ('makes HER commit adultery,' ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι). The Hebrew reads as case-law inside Deut 24 — על דבר נאוף echoing the statute's ערות דבר — the Greek as a new stricture upon it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:32): אם omitted in DGH; שכל] כל GH.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} you have heard{H8085} what was said{H559} to the ancients{H6931}: You shall not swear{H7650} by my name{H8034} falsely{H8267}, and you shall render{H7725} to YHWH{H3068} your oath{H7621}.

one_way_hebrew: The 'said to the ancients' here is real Torah, quoted: לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר is Lev 19:12 verbatim, and the second clause is the vow-payment law (Num 30:3; Deut 23:22; Ps 50:14, שלם לעליון נדריך). Greek Matthew's οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις ('you shall not perjure') paraphrases; the Hebrew cites the statutes themselves.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק י״ט (Perek 19) begins here. First ה״ of the chapter (see 1:22).
Howard's apparatus (5:33): לא] ולא EF; שבועתך] שבועתכם EF.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you not to swear{H7650} in any matter{H6045} vainly{H7723}: not by the heavens{H8064}, for it is the throne{H3678} of Elohim{H430};

one_way_hebrew: לשוא — the third commandment's own adverb (Exod 20:7, לא תשא את שם ה׳ אלקיך לשוא): the Hebrew forbids swearing 'in any matter VAINLY,' folding the saying back into the Decalogue's own terms; Greek's blanket μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως ('swear not at all') has lost the Decalogue anchor — and created a contradiction with the Torah's commanded oaths that the Hebrew never makes.
שמים כסא — Isa 66:1: השמים כסאי ('the heavens are my throne') — quoted on through the next verse.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:34): אלקים] אלהים A, אלים G; היא] הם ABDEFGH.

verses.translation: nor by the earth{H776}, for it is the footstool{H1916} of his feet{H7272}; nor by [Yerushalayim], for it is the city{H5892} of Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: Isa 66:1 continued: והארץ הדם רגלי ('and the earth is my footstool') — vv. 34-35 quote the throne-and-footstool verse whole, in order. עיר אלקים — 'the city of ELOHIM' (Ps 46:5; 48:2,9, עיר אלהים); Greek Matthew has 'the city of the great King' (Ps 48:3's other title). The Hebrew and the Greek each quote a psalm — different halves of the same psalm — but the Hebrew's phrase matches its own wording of Ps 48 elsewhere.
translation_notes: The base ms repeats בשמים ('by the heavens') by a copyist's slip where the sense requires בירושלים; mss ABEFG read בירושלם and Howard prints '(Jerusalem).' The transcription reads אליקים for the scan's אלקים; corrected.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:35): בשמים (2nd)] בירושלם ABEFG; ms D carries the Jerusalem clause at v. 37 instead.

verses.translation: Nor by your head{H7218}, for you cannot{H3201} make{H6213} one hair{H8181} white{H3836} or black{H7838}.

textual_notes: The ms writes א״ (the numeral 'one'), as at 5:19. Howard's apparatus (5:36): ולא] לא ABEFG; שלא] כי לא G; omitted by haplography in D.

verses.translation: But let your words{H1697} be{H1961} yes{H2005}, yes — and also no{H3808}, no. All{H3605} that is added{H3254} upon this{H2088} is evil{H7451}.

one_way_hebrew: הן הן... לא לא — the rabbinic dictum in its native form: שיהא הן שלך צדק ולאו שלך צדק ('let your yes be righteous and your no be righteous,' b. Bava Metsia 49a); mss BEF even read לאו לאו, the Talmud's own form of the word. Greek ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ transliterates the Hebrew idiom; James 5:12 carries the same Hebrew maxim into the epistles.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:37): לא לא] לאו לאו BEF; וגם] או ADEF, omit BG; זה] הזה D; ms D prefixes the Jerusalem clause here (see v. 35). The transcriber's footnote cites Jastrow (p. 347) on הן as 'yes.'

verses.translation: And again{H5750} you have heard{H8085} what is said{H559} in the Torah{H8451}: An eye{H5869} for{H8478} an eye, a tooth{H8127} for a tooth.

one_way_hebrew: 'What is said IN THE TORAH' — named as Torah and quoted exactly (Exod 21:24). The lex talionis is the judges' sentencing standard (Deut 19:18-21), given to the court, not to the avenger — which is exactly the distinction the next verse draws.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:38): ועוד] עוד H; שן תחת lost by haplography in EF.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: do not repay{H7999} evil{H7451} for{H8478} evil{H7451}; but he who strikes{H5221} you on your right{H3225} cheek{H3895} — prepare{H3559} for him the left{H8040}.

one_way_hebrew: לחי — the offered cheek of Lam 3:30 (יתן למכהו לחי — 'he gives his cheek to the smiter') and Isa 50:6; הכן — 'PREPARE for him the left': active, deliberate — the Hebrew of nonretaliation is hospitality to the blow, not passivity.
greek_deviations: 'Do not REPAY evil for evil' — not 'do not resist evil' (Greek μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ). The Hebrew is Prov 20:22 — אל תאמר אשלמה רע ('say not, I will REPAY evil') — and it is what the apostles themselves teach, in the same words: 'not rendering evil for evil' (Rom 12:17; 1 Thess 5:15; 1 Pet 3:9). The epistles agree with the HEBREW Matthew against Greek Matthew's wording: the earliest readers knew the saying in this form. What is renounced is private repayment (Lev 19:18's לא תקם), while v. 38's court standard stands.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:39): המכה] למכה ABDEFGH; רע תחת lost by haplography in DGH; הכן] תן G.

verses.translation: And whoever wishes{H7521} to contend{H2505} with you in court{H4941} and to rob{H1497} your tunic{H3801} — leave{H5800} him your robe{H4598}.

one_way_hebrew: כתנת... מעיל — the Torah's own two-garment pair (Exod 28:4, the priest's tunic and robe; 1 Sam 15:27; 24:5,12 — Saul's torn מעיל): inner and outer garment by their scriptural names, where Greek has χιτών/ἱμάτιον. And גזל (H1497) — Lev 19:13's robbery-verb (לא תגזל): the Hebrew names the lawsuit's aim as what the Torah forbids.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:40): כתניך] כתנתך CDGH; אליו] לו B.

verses.translation: And whoever asks{H7592} you to walk{H1980} with him a thousand{H505} paces — walk{H1980} with him two thousand{H505}.

one_way_hebrew: אלף פסיעות — 'a thousand PACES': the Roman mile IS mille passuum, 'a thousand paces' — the Hebrew renders Rome's road-unit by its literal Latin content, in the Mishnah's own step-word (פסיעה), where Greek simply borrows μίλιον. A Hebrew text among readers who live under Latin measures (see the Latin glosses at 2:11; 4:13; 5:31).
greek_deviations: ישאל — 'whoever ASKS you' (the base): even the request, not only the impressment, occasions the second mile; mss ABDEFG read יאנוס ('compels'), toward Greek ἀγγαρεύσει (the Persian corvée-word).
translation_notes: אלפיים — the transcription reads עלפיים; the scan reads אלפיים, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:41): ישאל] יאנוס ABDEFG; לילך] ללכת ABDG.

verses.translation: He who asks{H7592} of you — give{H5414} to him; and he who wishes{H7521} to borrow{H3867} from you — do not withhold{H4513}.

one_way_hebrew: אל תמנע — Prov 3:27's own opening: אל תמנע טוב מבעליו ('withhold not good from them to whom it is due'). And לוה — the Torah's lending vocabulary (Deut 15:7-10, the commanded loan; Ps 37:26). The generosity here is the Torah's commanded charity, stated in Proverbs' imperative.
translation_notes: אל — the transcription reads על; the scan reads אל, corrected here.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: You have heard{H8085} what was said{H559} to the ancients{H6931}: You shall love{H157} the one who loves you, and hate{H8130} the one who hates you{H8130}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew does NOT put Lev 19:18 in the mouth of 'the ancients.' What 'was said' is a folk-maxim of reciprocity — 'love your LOVER and hate your HATER' (לאוהבך... לשונאך) — not 'love your NEIGHBOR (רעך) and hate your enemy.' Greek Matthew half-quotes Lev 19:18 and welds 'hate thine enemy' onto it, leaving readers to think the Torah taught hatred — a command the Torah nowhere gives (it commands the opposite: Exod 23:4-5; Prov 25:21). The Hebrew's target is the proverb of reciprocity; the Torah's own words are never misquoted. The אוהב/שונא wordplay then runs through vv. 44-46.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק כ׳ (Perek 20) begins here.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: love{H157} your enemies{H341}, and do{H6213} good{H2896} to the one who hates you{H8130} and provokes you{H3707}, and pray{H6419} for your pursuers{H7291} and your oppressors{H3905},
words: to the one who hates you

one_way_hebrew: ולוחציכם — לחץ, the Torah's oppression-verb (Exod 22:20; 23:9 — 'you shall not OPPRESS the stranger, for you were strangers'): pray for those doing to you what Egypt did to Israel. And רודפיכם resumes the beatitudes' chain (vv. 9-12) — the pursued pray for the pursuers.
greek_deviations: The full four-fold form — love / do good / pray; enemies, haters, provokers, pursuers, oppressors — matches Luke 6:27-28 ('do good to them that hate you... pray for them which despitefully use you') against the short text of Greek Matthew's oldest copies. And within the Shem Tov tradition itself, mss BDEFG drop everything after 'love your enemies' — the assimilation toward the short Greek text caught in the act.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:44): ועשו . . . ולוחציכם omitted in BDEFG; ואני] אני B; אויביכם] לאויבכם A; ולוחציכם] ולוחצכם A; רודפיכם] רודפכם A; בשביל] בעד A.

verses.translation: so that{H4616} you may be{H1961} sons{H1121} of your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}, who makes his sun{H8121} rise{H2224} on good{H2896} and evil{H7451}, and rains{H4305} on the wicked{H7563} and the righteous{H6662}.

one_way_hebrew: רשעים וצדיקים — the fixed Hebrew pair of Gen 18:23-25 ('wilt thou destroy the RIGHTEOUS with the WICKED?') — the same pair this text supplies at 24:40. Greek δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους ('just and unjust') narrows the moral pair to a legal one. מזריח and ממטיר — the causatives of providence (Gen 2:5, המטיר; Job 38:26-27): the Father's daily benefaction stated in creation's own verbs.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:45): BDEFG prefix a dittograph of vv. 44-45a; G reorders 'on the evil and on the good.'

verses.translation: If you love{H157} those who love you, what{H335} reward{H7939} is yours? Do not the brazen{H5794}-faced{H6440} love those who love them?

greek_deviations: 'Do not even the BRAZEN-FACED (עזי פנים) love their lovers?' — Greek has 'the tax collectors' (τελῶναι). עז פנים is the Hebrew's own moral category: the fierce-faced nation of Deut 28:50, the brazen woman of Prov 7:13 — and the rabbis' exact pairing, עז פנים לגיהנם ('the brazen-faced is for Gehinnom,' Avot 5:20), the very destination this chapter's judgments name (vv. 22, 29-30). The Greek points at a despised trade; the Hebrew names the character-type its own tradition sends to Gehinnom.
textual_notes: GREEK 5:47 HAS NO COUNTERPART IN THE SHEM TOV TEXT: Howard's apparatus — 'vs 47] omit all mss' — and his English runs directly from v. 46 to v. 48. No 'and if you greet your brothers only...' in any of the nine mss. (The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries a form of it: 'And if you meet with shalom your brothers only, do not the governors of the Notsrim do this thing?')
Howard's apparatus (5:46): אוהביהם] אוהבהם A; אוהביכם] אוהבכם A.

verses.translation: Be{H1961}, you, perfect{H8549}, as{H834} your Father{H1} is perfect{H8535}.

one_way_hebrew: 'Be TAMIM as your Father is TAM' — the closing sentence re-speaks the Torah's own command: תמים תהיה עם יהוה אלהיך ('you shall be PERFECT with YHWH your God,' Deut 18:13) and Gen 17:1 (התהלך לפני והיה תמים). And תם is Job's title (איש תם, Job 1:1,8). The sermon that opened by upholding every letter and point of the Torah (vv. 17-19) closes by quoting the Torah's command of wholeness — Greek τέλειοι translates it; the Hebrew commands it in Moshe's word.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew has simply 'your Father' — no 'heavenly' (Greek ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος).
translation_notes: The base ms spells תמיהים (a stray yod — as written it would mean 'astonished'); all other mss read תמימים ('perfect'), which the sense and the Deut 18:13 source require; Howard prints 'Be you (perfect).' The translation follows תמימים; the words preserve the ms spelling.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (5:48): תמיהים] תמימים ABCDEFG.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 5 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is a Torah-sermon in halakhic Hebrew, and its differences from the Greek run through every section. (1) The beatitudes are fewer and Hebrew to the bone: 5:3 and 5:5 are missing from the base ms (Howard prints them in parentheses from ms A); Greek 5:6-7 exist in NO Shem Tov ms ('vs 6/7] omit all mss'); and 5:4 reads 'happy are those who WAIT (החוכים), for they shall be comforted' — Isa 30:18's beatitude answered by Isa 40:1, not 'those who mourn.' 5:9-11 hinge on one root: רודפי שלום ('pursuers of peace,' Ps 34:15) become הנרדפים ('the pursued') — a catchword chain Greek cannot carry. (2) 5:14-15: 'you are the MAOR (luminary, Gen 1:14-16) of the world... set on the MENORAH' — the Sanctuary's lamp, not a generic stand. (3) 5:17-19 run on Num 30's legal pair: 'I came not to ANNUL (להפר) Torah but to COMPLETE it'; 'one letter or one POINT shall not be annulled from the Torah OR THE PROPHETS, for everything shall be ESTABLISHED (יתקיים)'; the transgressor-teacher is a 'son of hevel' and the UPHOLDER (המקיים) is great — annulment versus confirmation, not abolition versus piety; ms A's יוד for אות shows the Hebrew pull inside the tradition. (4) 5:21-30: Mishnah-form liability (חייב) with graded courts; no 'Raca' — Hebrew פחות and שוטה; 5:28 reads the seventh commandment through the tenth (ויחמוד, Exod 20:17) and the base has 'in HER heart'; 5:29's eye 'ENTICES' (יסיתך — Deut 13:7's apostasy-verb); 5:25's debtor goes to Joseph's בית הסוהר down to 'the last perutah.' (5) 5:31-32 command the get: 'whoever leaves his wife MUST GIVE her a get of severance' (Deut 24:1 upheld, glossed in Latin: libel repudio) and 'HE is the adulterer' — the guilt on the dismissing man, not the woman. (6) 5:33-37 quote Lev 19:12 verbatim, forbid swearing לשוא (the third commandment's own adverb — no blanket ban contradicting the Torah's commanded oaths), quote Isa 66:1's throne-and-footstool whole, and end in the Talmud's own maxim (הן הן... לא לא; BEF even read לאו לאו). (7) 5:38-42: 'what is said IN THE TORAH — eye for eye' stands as the court's standard, and what is forbidden is Prov 20:22's private repayment — 'do not REPAY evil for evil,' the very wording the apostles use (Rom 12:17; 1 Thess 5:15) against Greek Matthew's 'resist not evil'; the second mile is אלף פסיעות — the Roman mille passuum rendered literally. (8) 5:43 refuses to blame the Torah: 'the ancients' said 'love your LOVER and hate your HATER' — a folk-proverb, not Lev 19:18; 5:44's full Luke-like form ('do good... pray for your pursuers and OPPRESSORS' — לחץ, Exod 22:20) is cut back to the short Greek text by BDEFG; 5:46 has 'the brazen-faced' (עזי פנים — Avot's עז פנים לגיהנם) for Greek's 'tax collectors'; Greek 5:47 is absent from all mss. (9) 5:48 closes on Deut 18:13: 'Be TAMIM as your Father is TAM.' Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 13), 13 (14), 20 (15), 25 (16), 27 (17), 31 (18), 33 (19), and 43 (20).
